Guidance & outlook: Banking, we had called out that we would see a sharp recovery going into the next quarter, and that's what's reflected in the sequential numbers of 13.5%.
On the margins, the highlight is we are progressing well on margins and are well on our target to meet a full-year reported EBITDA of 17.1%-17.4%.
Of the same, $6.5 million dollars was paid, and you would have expected that for an asset in the data space, the targets that we set were very ambitious.
Growth & demand: As a consequence of the one-offs our ETR came down and our EBITDA, in absolute terms, while it grew solidly at 19.4% YoY, our EPS grew even faster.
From an overall revenue perspective, we had a good quarter with a YoY growth being 8.6%, as you can see that the growth was led by five out of the six verticals delivering YoY growth.
The key to highlight here is that our IT business is growing at a much faster pace than the company average, and the IT services growth is close to 9%, while BPS is at 4.7%.
Margins & costs: Current quarter saw a margin improvement of 50 bps on a reported basis, and the margin increase was driven by an operational improvement of 100 bps with the improvement in utilization, offshore mix, and some bit of a tailwind from calendar.
That's what we said, that despite the fact that we have taken the 15 bps of headwind in terms of the cost in the current quarter, we still are at 17.2% from a reported EBITDA perspective.

On an LTM basis, the OCF to EBITDA is at 76%, higher than the target that we have set for ourselves at 70%, so we'll continue to work in terms of continuing to deliver 70% plus on an LTM basis on OCF to EBITDA.
Capex & expansion: The most important event for us from a business perspective was the acquisition of SMC.
Our acquisition is still the lowest or amongst the lowest in the industry.
The Softcrylic acquisition which we did last year, had a first year earnout of $25 million.
Risks & challenges: This was partially offset with currency headwind of 35 bps and one-time charges of 15 bps.
If you net out all of this, it's a headwind from a PnL perspective of close to $500K, which turns out to be close to 15 bps.
FS, like Vikash pointed out, in spite of what we called out as a 1% headwind for the company, will translate that to a 3%-4% headwind for FS.
